Propagate

/PROP-uh-gayt/ - the stress falls on PROP · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Propagate means to multiply, spread out.

A single doctored screenshot can propagate through three group chats before breakfast.

Worked Example

Left alone, the pond's duckweed will propagate until the surface reads solid green: each floating leaf splits into two, two into four, and by the second week the koi are invisible.

Propagate covers both halves of spreading: living things multiplying themselves, and ideas, signals, or errors being passed outward copy by copy. Either way the heart of it is generation — what propagates doesn't just travel, it reproduces as it goes.

How Propagate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

disseminate

disseminate: to scatter information deliberately and widely; propagate adds self-multiplication — each copy seeds more

reproduce

reproduce: to make a new copy or a new generation; propagate stresses the spreading that follows

Antonyms

contain

contain: to keep something from spreading past a boundary

curb

curb: to check or restrain something's growth

How Strong Is It? — spread → disseminate → propagate

spread vs. propagate

spread vs. propagate: Spread stops short of propagate — what spreads gets around, but nothing new is being made along the way.

disseminate vs. propagate

disseminate vs. propagate: Disseminate stops short of propagate — disseminating scatters copies from one source, while propagating sets every copy to breeding copies of its own.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of propagate.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pro-

Prefix — pro-: forward

Root — pag

Root — pag: to fasten, to fix (Latin pangere)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make, to do (verb-forming)

Put it together

Put it together: Pro- ('forward') + pag- (Latin pangere, 'to fasten') + -ate = to fasten forward. A propago was a vine-layer: a shoot bent down and pinned into the soil to root as a new plant. Roman gardeners fastened plants forward one pin at a time; the word now covers everything that spreads by making more of itself.

Use the root in a new word: pact

Use the root in a new word: pact: The rival unions signed a pact to strike together or not at all.

Root Check

Word Choice

technical / neutral

Propagate is the word of gardeners, physicists, and network engineers — cuttings, waves, and updates all propagate. In loose talk 'spread' will do; choose propagate when the thing multiplies or transmits itself step by step. Plans and gossip are usually spread; species, signals, and errors propagate.
